maturity_states.definition: Understands what the competency is and why it matters.
Has completed structured learning relevant to the competency.
Has used the skill in a controlled or supervised exercise.
Has produced observable work or performance using the competency.
A qualified reviewer has confirmed independent performance meets the standard.
Has used the competency successfully in an authentic setting.
Can consistently perform the competency and successfully guide or review others.

competencies.name: Self-Direction
competencies.definition: Sets goals, identifies next steps, manages commitments, reflects on progress, and asks for help appropriately.

competencies.name: Communication
competencies.definition: Communicates clearly through speaking, writing, listening, and presentation for the intended audience.

competencies.name: Collaboration
competencies.definition: Works reliably with others, manages disagreement, shares responsibility, and documents commitments.

competencies.name: Research Literacy
competencies.definition: Finds information, distinguishes claims from evidence, and recognizes source quality and limitations.

competencies.name: Digital Fluency
competencies.definition: Uses accounts, files, collaboration systems, AI, and common professional tools responsibly and efficiently.

competencies.name: Civic & Institutional Literacy
competencies.definition: Understands how government, nonprofit, educational, and commercial institutions operate and interact.

competencies.name: Professional Practice
competencies.definition: Demonstrates reliability, confidentiality, meeting discipline, documentation, deadlines, and appropriate workplace conduct.

competencies.name: Safety & Resilience
competencies.definition: Recognizes hazards, escalation paths, emergency roles, and basic continuity responsibilities.

competencies.name: Project Management
competencies.definition: Converts an objective into scope, tasks, owners, milestones, risks, and deliverables.

competencies.name: Ethics, Consent & Privacy
competencies.definition: Identifies ethical and privacy implications and obtains appropriate consent before collecting, using, or sharing information.

competencies.name: Data Literacy
competencies.definition: Reads, organizes, analyzes, and communicates quantitative or structured information without overstating conclusions.

competencies.name: Documentation & Provenance
competencies.definition: Maintains traceable records showing where information, decisions, and artifacts came from.

competencies.name: Facilitation & Meetings
competencies.definition: Plans and leads productive meetings, captures decisions, and turns conversation into accountable follow-up.

competencies.name: Accessible & Inclusive Practice
competencies.definition: Produces experiences and materials usable by diverse people and recognizes accessibility barriers.

competencies.name: Community Engagement
competencies.definition: Builds respectful two-way relationships with residents and community stakeholders instead of treating engagement as broadcast outreach.

competencies.name: Service Navigation
competencies.definition: Finds and explains public, nonprofit, and community resources and helps people navigate them accurately.

competencies.name: Stakeholder Coordination
competencies.definition: Maps organizations, responsibilities, relationships, and commitments around a shared issue or project.

competencies.name: Public Program Delivery
competencies.definition: Helps operate a community-facing service using defined procedures, privacy rules, documentation, and quality controls.

competencies.name: Emergency & Incident Coordination
competencies.definition: Understands incident roles, chain of command, resource coordination, and communication during organized emergency response.

competencies.name: Research Design
competencies.definition: Turns a question into a defensible research plan with methods, scope, limitations, and evidence requirements.

competencies.name: Source Evaluation
competencies.definition: Evaluates authority, methodology, recency, provenance, conflicts, and limitations of sources.

competencies.name: Human Research Methods
competencies.definition: Conducts interviews, surveys, or other human-participant research with appropriate consent and ethical safeguards.

competencies.name: Evidence Synthesis
competencies.definition: Connects multiple sources to claims while preserving disagreements, uncertainty, and evidentiary strength.

competencies.name: Policy Analysis
competencies.definition: Describes policy alternatives, implementation mechanisms, affected populations, costs, tradeoffs, and evidence without substituting advocacy for analysis.

competencies.name: Publication & Citation
competencies.definition: Produces reviewable, attributable work with citations, revisions, version control, and publication-ready provenance.

competencies.name: Opportunity Discovery
competencies.definition: Identifies real workforce, business, or organizational problems worth solving and distinguishes them from imagined demand.

competencies.name: User / Customer Discovery
competencies.definition: Conducts structured discovery to understand needs, constraints, and decision criteria without leading the participant.

competencies.name: Offer & Scope Design
competencies.definition: Converts a validated need into a clearly defined product, service, project scope, or role with deliverables and boundaries.

competencies.name: Financial & Operational Basics
competencies.definition: Understands basic budgeting, pricing and cost concepts, resource requirements, operational constraints, and simple business metrics.

competencies.name: Client / Project Delivery
competencies.definition: Manages expectations, communicates status, controls scope, and delivers accepted work.

competencies.name: Workforce & Career Navigation
competencies.definition: Builds a credible professional record and navigates applications, interviews, apprenticeships, employers, and advancement pathways.

competencies.name: Story & Message Development
competencies.definition: Defines audience, purpose, narrative structure, facts, and communication objective before production begins.

competencies.name: Capture & Production
competencies.definition: Produces usable audio, photo, video, or other media with appropriate planning and technical execution.

competencies.name: Editing & Post-Production
competencies.definition: Transforms raw materials into coherent finished media while maintaining factual and technical integrity.

competencies.name: Verification, Rights & Licensing
competencies.definition: Verifies claims and media origins and handles releases, permissions, copyright, and licensing appropriately.

competencies.name: Publication, Distribution & Audience
competencies.definition: Publishes through appropriate channels, preserves lineage, and evaluates reach or response without confusing attention with impact.

competencies.name: Systems Thinking
competencies.definition: Understands how technical, human, institutional, and physical components interact and how changes propagate through a system.

competencies.name: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
competencies.definition: Practices identity, access, data protection, threat awareness, and secure operational behavior.

competencies.name: Spatial Intelligence
competencies.definition: Interprets geographic, temporal, and infrastructure data and uses spatial tools appropriately while respecting provenance and access restrictions.

competencies.name: Infrastructure & Energy Literacy
competencies.definition: Understands the basic operation and interdependence of energy, transportation, communications, water, buildings, and related infrastructure.

competencies.name: Operational Decision Support
competencies.definition: Converts evidence and live operational context into bounded options, risks, priorities, and actionable information for decision-makers.

competencies.name: Automation & Tooling
competencies.definition: Uses automation, APIs, AI, or other technical tools to improve workflows while preserving security, reviewability, and human authority.
